Extremos quoque fratrum suorum quinque viros constituit coram rege:
Likewise, he stood in the sight of the king five men, the last of his brothers.
Ad peregrinandum in terra tua venimus:
We came to sojourn in your land,
quoniam non est herba gregibus servorum tuorum,
because there is no grass for the flocks of your servants,
the famine being very grievous in the land of Canaan.
petimusque ut esse nos jubeas servos tuos in terra Gessen.
And we petition you that you may order us, your servants, to be in the land of Goshen.”
And so the king said to Joseph:
Pater tuus et fratres tui venerunt ad te.
“Your father and brothers have come to you.
Terra Ægypti in conspectu tuo est:
The land of Egypt is in your sight.
in optimo loco fac eos habitare,
Cause them to live in the best place,
and deliver to them the land of Goshen.
Quod si nosti in eis esse viros industrios,
And if you know there to be industrious men among them,
appoint these as foremen over my cattle.”
Post hæc introduxit Joseph patrem suum ad regem,
After this, Joseph brought in his father to the king,
et statuit eum coram eo: qui benedicens illi,
and he stood him in his sight. He blessed him,
Quot sunt dies annorum vitæ tuæ?
“How many are the days of the years of your life?”
Dies peregrinationis meæ centum triginta annorum sunt,
“The days of my sojourn are one hundred and thirty years,
et non pervenerunt usque ad dies patrum meorum quibus peregrinati sunt.
and they do not reach even to the days of the sojourning of my fathers.”
Joseph vero patri et fratribus suis dedit possessionem in Ægypto in optimo terræ loco,
Truly, Joseph gave his father and brothers a possession in Egypt, in the best place of the land,
along with all his father’s house,
providing portions of food to each one.
In toto enim orbe panis deerat,
For in the whole world there was a lack of bread,
and a famine had oppressed the land,
most of all Egypt and Canaan,
E quibus omnem pecuniam congregavit pro venditione frumenti,
from which he gathered together all the money for the grain that they bought,
et intulit eam in ærarium regis.
and he took it into the treasury of the king.
And when the buyers had run out of money,
Why should we die in your sight,
et dabo vobis pro eis cibos,
and I will give food to you in exchange for them,
if you do not have money.”
And when they had brought them,
he gave them food for their horses,
sustentavitque eos illo anno pro commutatione pecorum.
And he sustained them in that year in exchange for their cattle.
Non celabimus dominum nostrum quod deficiente pecunia,
“We will not conceal from our lord that our money is gone;
quod absque corporibus et terra nihil habeamus.
Neither are you unaware that we have nothing left but our bodies and our land.
why should you watch us die?
Both we and our land will be yours.
ne pereunte cultore redigatur terra in solitudinem.
lest by the dying off of cultivators the land be reduced to a wilderness.”
Emit igitur Joseph omnem terram Ægypti,
Therefore, Joseph bought all the land of Egypt,
vendentibus singulis possessiones suas præ magnitudine famis.
each one selling his possessions because of the magnitude of the famine.
And he subjected it to Pharaoh,
et cunctos populos ejus a novissimis terminis Ægypti usque ad extremos fines ejus,
along with all of its people, from the newest borders of Egypt, even to its furthest limits,
except the land of the priests,
quæ a rege tradita fuerat eis:
which had been delivered to them by the king.
quibus et statuta cibaria ex horreis publicis præbebantur,
To these also a portion of food was supplied out of the public storehouses,
et idcirco non sunt compulsi vendere possessiones suas.
and, for this reason, they were not compelled to sell their possessions.

only let our lord look kindly upon us,

Ex eo tempore usque in præsentem diem,
From that time, even to the present day,
in universa terra Ægypti regibus quinta pars solvitur,
in the entire land of Egypt, the fifth part is turned over to the kings,
et factum est quasi in legem,
and it has become like a law,
except in the land of the priests,
quæ libera ab hac conditione fuit.

Cumque appropinquare cerneret diem mortis suæ,
And when he discerned that the day of his death was approaching,
Si inveni gratiam in conspectu tuo,
“If I have found favor in your sight,
pone manum tuam sub femore meo:
place your hand under my thigh.
et facies mihi misericordiam et veritatem,
And you shall show me mercy and truth,
ut non sepelias me in Ægypto:
not to bury me in Egypt.
But I shall sleep with my fathers,
et auferas me de terra hac,
